# dm/third_party: third-party code

This is code written by others, shipped with the repository so there is nothing to download. Each component keeps its original license, and the license file sits in its own directory.

| Directory | What it is | Version and changes | Where it is used | License file |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bcdec/` | BC1-BC7 block decoder, a single header `bcdec.h` | 0.985 (upstream commit `80859ed`), signed BC4 / BC5 endpoints read as `signed char` (`char` is unsigned on ARM) | Android: decodes BC textures on the CPU on devices without BC textures (`dm/android/gfx_vk_tex.c` `bc_decode`) | `bcdec/LICENSE` (MIT or the Unlicense, your choice) |
| `flip/` | NVIDIA FLIP, an image difference metric that models human viewing. `FLIP.h` plus the source of the command-line tool in `tool/` | Not recorded in the directory | Verification: the image quality measurements in `dm/verify/gfxq/`; build `flip` first with `make -C dm/third_party/flip` | `flip/LICENSE` (BSD 3-Clause) |
| `dav1d/` | The AV1 decoder dav1d: the C sources, headers and arm64 NEON assembly an arm64 build compiles, with the configuration meson generates in `config/` and per-bit-depth wrappers of its templates in `config/tmpl/` | 1.5.4 (upstream commit `54706fc`), unmodified; one file of ours, `config/android/config.h` (the ELF configuration: no symbol prefix, `getauxval`) | Host: decodes the games' AV1 movies where VideoToolbox has no AV1 decoder (`dm/host/hle_movie_av1.c`), and every AV1 movie on Android. `dm/host/Makefile` builds it into `gen/dav1d/libdav1d.a`; the iOS build compiles the same files; `dm/android/build.py` compiles them with `config/android` first (its assembly is ELF already, not converted) | `dav1d/COPYING` (BSD 2-Clause) |
| `libvpx/` | The VP8 and VP9 decoders from libvpx: the 116 source files a decoder-only build compiles, their headers, and the generated configuration in `config/` | v1.17.0 (upstream commit `6df3ec3`), unmodified | Host: decodes the games' VP8 and VP9 movies (`dm/host/hle_movie.c`, the Switch 2's `nn::codec` decoders in `dm/host/hle_codec_video.c`). `dm/host/Makefile` builds it into `gen/vpx/libvpx.a`; the iOS build and `dm/android/build.py` compile the same files | `libvpx/LICENSE` (BSD 3-Clause), with the patent grant in `libvpx/PATENTS` |
| `stb_vorbis/` | Ogg Vorbis decoder, a single file `stb_vorbis.c` | 1.22 (upstream commit `1ee679c`), unmodified | Host: decodes the Vorbis sound tracks of the games' WebM movies (`dm/host/hle_movie.c`, which includes the file with its push-data API only) | `stb_vorbis/LICENSE` (MIT or public domain, your choice; the same text ends `stb_vorbis.c`) |
| `ryujinx/` | The shader translation library from Ryujinx, three projects: `Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader`, `Ryujinx.Common`, `Spv.Generator` | Ryujinx 1.3.2, with the local changes listed in `ryujinx/README.md` | Referenced by the shader translation tool `dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_xlate`, which translates the original Switch shaders to SPIR-V | `ryujinx/LICENSE.txt` (MIT); `ryujinx/src/Spv.Generator/LICENSE` is that subproject's own license text |
| `vulkan-headers/` | The Vulkan C headers: `vulkan_core.h`, `vk_platform.h`, `vulkan_vi.h` and the `vk_video/` headers they include | Vulkan-Headers 1.4.363, unmodified | Host: the Vulkan layer on Metal (`dm/gfx/vk/hle_vk.m`) that runs Hades | `vulkan-headers/LICENSE.md` (Apache-2.0 or MIT, your choice) |

A few more notes:

- `flip/tool/` also carries three single-header libraries used by the FLIP command-line tool: `stb_image.h` (2.23), `stb_image_write.h` (1.13) and `tinyexr.h`. Their license notices are in the files themselves.
- `bcdec/README.md`, `dav1d/README.md`, `libvpx/README.md`, `stb_vorbis/README.md`, `ryujinx/README.md` and `vulkan-headers/README.md` record where each came from and what it is used for.
- Five pieces of third-party code live outside this directory: `dm/gfx/nvn/include/nvn.h` (MIT, author named in the file header), the layout size algorithm in `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_tex.c`, ported from deko3d (zlib license), and two adapted from MacNativeGames (MIT, license text in `macnativegames/LICENSE`): in `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m` the GPU widening of 8-bit indices (`wide_*`) and the in-pass clear triangles (`clear_color_tri` / `clear_ds_tri`), from its `widen_u8_gpu` and `clear_quad` / `clear_ds_quad`, and the Tears of the Kingdom visibility-counter lowering in `dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_xlate/Program.cs` (`VertexCounterLowering`). The fifth is AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 1 (MIT, license text in `dm/android/shaders/fsr/LICENSE`): its EASU and RCAS, ported in `dm/android/shaders/fsr/fsr1.glsl` for the present's upscaling passes (`dm/android/gfx_vk_fsr.c`; the changes are listed at the top of the file) and mirrored on the CPU by `fsr1_ref.c` beside it.
